sentences.text: Orientognathus is a genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now China.
Its lower jaw features a slightly pointed, toothless front, while the rest of the jaw holds straight, relatively robust, and long teeth.

The fourth metacarpal bone measures 38% of the humerus length, the ulna is shorter than any wing phalanges, and the tibia is almost as long as the femur. The pteroid wing bone is 21% of the humerus length with an expanded tip, and the deltopectoral crest on the humerus is not very developed.
It stands as the largest known Rhamphorhynchinae from the Late Jurassic of China and remains the only known pterosaur from the Tithonian stage of that country.

The genus is known from a single specimen containing most of the skeleton and skull, which was first named and described in 2015 by Lü Junchang and colleagues. The species Orientognathus chaoyangensis was named by Lü Junchang, Hanyong Pu, Xu Li, Wei Xufang, Huali Chang, and Martin Kundrát. The holotype specimen, 41HIII-0418, was found in western Liaoning province within the Tuchengzi Formation, dated to the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 150 million years ago.

The genus name derives from the Latin word oriens, referring to its origin in East Asia, and the Ancient Greek word gnathos, meaning "jaw." The species name refers to the location where the fossil was found, Chaoyang.

Phylogenetic analysis determined that Orientognathus was a basal member of the family Rhamphorhynchidae, possibly belonging to the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae. The parent group of Orientognathus is Rhamphorhynchinae, and it belongs to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.

The fossil was found in the Upper Jurassic Tuchengzi Formation of China, a layer slightly younger than the Tiaojishan Formation where other regional pterosaurs are found. The time range for Orientognathus is the Berriasian, from 143.1 to 137.05 million years ago.
